arcs.description: A CLI write records what the caller authored, or it refuses.
arcs.intent:
A CLI write records what the caller authored, or it refuses. Four separate defects measured in a single week share one shape: a `storytree` write path returns success while the durable record it stored differs from what the caller wrote — and the divergence is invisible unless someone deliberately reads the row back.

The four, each measured rather than reasoned about:

- `library artifact retire --reason "@<file>"` and `library graduate park --reason "@<file>"` store the LITERAL `@path` string as the record. Four park records in `graduation-park.json` hold nothing but a path into a per-sessi…
arcs.endState:
A CLI write either records what the caller authored, or it refuses and says why. Success and fidelity stop being independent.

The four measured instances are closed: `@path` is expanded once at the flag-parsing boundary rather than per callsite, and an unresolvable `@` value is refused; an explicitly passed id that would be truncated is refused instead of silently sliced; `sync-corpus --pg` skips and reports a seed artifact whose latest live event is a more recent deletion; and every CLI store-write call site is mechanically checked to carry branch attribution.

arcs.intent:
Make the pathways between story nodes first-class: give an edge an identity, an address, and a place in the claim namespace, so that the glue between two stories can be named, inspected, owned and claimed the same way a node can — and, before any of that is built, give the factory the instrument that can tell whether anyone actually contends on it.

THE OWNER'S DIRECTION, AND WHAT MEASUREMENT DID TO ITS JUSTIFICATION. The owner proposed this on 2026-08-05: "i was thinking that the pathways/edges between story nodes probably needs to behave like a its own node that can be claimed". The structu…
arcs.endState:
An edge between two story nodes is a first-class object: it has a stable derived address, it can be listed and inspected from the CLI, it resolves in a TYPED claim namespace that refuses ids naming nothing, and a session holding it is visible on the map along the trail the edge already draws.
